title: How far can ten fingers count?
hook: Ten fingers, each up or down. How many different numbers can they show?

doesNotKnow: that n two-state places count 2^n different numbers

misconception: Ten fingers can show only ten numbers, or at most a hundred.
objective: The learner can explain that each up-or-down finger doubles the number of patterns, so ten fingers worth 1, 2, 4 ... 512 show every number from 0 to 1023: 1024 numbers.

claims.text: Ten fingers worth 1, 2, 4, ..., 512 add up to 1023 when all are up, the largest number and the last cell of the grid.
claims.source: 1 + 2 + ... + 512 = 2^10 - 1 = 1023; recomputed with node from the stage's VALUES. | REOPENED 2026-10-14 (v3, wave D r5 revision by demo-builder): learner-visible sentence changed; needs a fresh check. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own node: sum of VALUES = 1023 = 2^10-1; cell 1023 is row 15, column 63 of the 64x16 grid (last cell).

claims.text: Ten fingers, each up or down, make 2^10 = 1024 different patterns.
claims.source: Each finger has 2 states independently: 2 x 2 x ... x 2 (ten times) = 1024.

claims.text: Every whole number from 0 to 1023 has exactly one finger pattern (its binary representation); counting up one at a time, each new pattern lands on a new number, none skipped and none twice.
claims.source: Existence and uniqueness of binary representation, by induction on the number of places; 1024 patterns and 1024 numbers match one to one. | REOPENED 2026-10-14 (v3, wave D r5 revision by demo-builder): learner-visible sentence changed; needs a fresh check. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Own node: the 1024 patterns give 1024 distinct sums 0..1023. Counting +1 visits n+1 each time, so no skip or repeat.

claims.text: Adding one more finger doubles the count: it can be down (all the old numbers) or up (each old number plus its value); ten doublings give 2 × 2 × … × 2 = 1024.
claims.source: Patterns with n + 1 places = 2 x patterns with n places. | REOPENED 2026-10-14 (v3, wave D r5 revision by demo-builder): learner-visible sentence changed; needs a fresh check. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Doubling argument correct; 2^10 = 1024.

claims.text: Counting from 0 to 15 uses only the four right fingers (worth 1, 2, 4, 8), 16 numbers; at 16 the finger worth 16 goes up and the four right fingers start again from all down.
claims.source: 15 = 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 is the largest sum of the four right fingers; 16 = 10000 in binary. Stage caption at 16 in Demo.tsx. | Added 2026-10-14 (v3) by demo-builder. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): 8+4+2+1 = 15; 16 = 10000 in binary; stage caption at 16 matches.

claims.text: The grid has one cell per number from 0 (top left) to 1023 (bottom right), lit when the learner has made that number; 'Numbers made' counts the lit cells.
claims.source: The lesson's own display in Demo.tsx (64 × 16 grid, made set). | Added 2026-10-14 (v3) by demo-builder. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 22): Demo.tsx: 1024 cells, cell k is number k, made-set cells lit; 'Numbers made' = made.size. Current number is drawn in a darker shade but is in the set.

recall.question: Using only 8 up-or-down switches worth 1, 2, 4 ... 128, how many different numbers (0 included) can you set?
recall.why: Each switch doubles the count: 2 multiplied by itself 8 times is 256, covering 0 to 255.
